opportunities.title: Green Climate Fund funding proposals through the CGIAR System Organization (GCF-accredited entity)
opportunities.program: GCF funded activities (funding proposals; Simplified Approval Process / Project Preparation Facility as applicable) via accredited entity 'CGIAR System Organization'
opportunities.deadline_text: No call deadline; funding proposals are submitted by accredited entities on a continuous basis. AE page: 'Re-accreditation submission deadline: 29 Mar 2027'; 'Renewal date: 29 Sep 2027'; 'Term end date: 29 Sep 2027'.
opportunities.funding_text: Accreditation scope listed by GCF: 'Size: Small'; 'ESS Category: Category C, Intermediation 3'; 'Fiduciary Standards: Basic, Project management, Grant award'. No per-project amount on the AE page; FP304 amount not listed there.
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Only GCF accredited entities submit funding proposals. CGIAR System Organization is accredited (Status: Accredited; Type: International; Country: France (Montpellier)); CGIAR centers would develop/execute projects under it.
opportunities.eligible_countries: GCF-eligible developing countries (NDA no-objection is a standard GCF rule, not restated on the AE page).
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Re-verified 2026-11-02: 'CGIAR System Organization (CGIAR)' remains Accredited (approved 19 Oct 2018; AMA executed 21 Sep 2022, effective 30 Sep 2022; term end/renewal 29 Sep 2027; re-accreditation submission deadline 29 Mar 2027). One project listed: FP304 LARACI (Cote d'Ivoire), 'Under implementation'. No individual CGIAR center is separately accredited. Route for the Alliance: co-develop with an NDA and submit through the CGIAR System Organization (Small, Category C, grant-award scope only), or serve as executing/technical partner of another AE (FAO, IFAD, UNDP, WFP, CAF, CABEI, IDB, national DAEs). Key risk: accreditation term ends 29 Sep 2027 unless re-accreditation is submitted by 29 Mar 2027.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Accredited entity (CGIAR System Organization) as lead; NDA no-objection; project must fit the AE's accreditation scope (Small, Category C, grant award).
opportunities.consortium_details: Accredited entity + NDA (country ownership) + executing entities (CGIAR centers, national institutions).
opportunities.eligible_activities: Climate adaptation and mitigation projects in GCF result areas (e.g., food and water security, livelihoods, ecosystems, forests and land use).
opportunities.required_documents: Standard GCF concept note / funding proposal package (FP304 documents on the AE page: concept note, funding proposal, gender assessment, gender action plan).
opportunities.application_procedure: Engage the CGIAR System Organization GCF focal point and the target country's NDA; submit concept note via the GCF Partner Portal through the AE; optionally request Project Preparation Facility support.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Climate-resilient agri-food systems and land management (cf. FP304) use climate risk analytics, EO monitoring and crop modelling directly; methods are components rather than the main output.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Only verified direct route from CGIAR to GCF; large-scale, country-owned adaptation programmes in LAC/Africa/Asia fit the Alliance mission.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Alliance can deliver climate-information/EO/advisory components, but GCF project development takes 1-3 years, needs NDA buy-in and System-level coordination; accreditation renewal due Sep 2027.
opportunities.recommendation: Pursue as a medium-term pipeline; first confirm with the CGIAR System Organization that re-accreditation will be submitted by 29 Mar 2027, otherwise plan via another AE (FAO/IFAD/WFP/CAF).
opportunities.potential_partners: CGIAR System Organization (AE); NDAs; national meteorological services; FAO/IFAD/WFP as alternative AEs; CIFOR-ICRAF (FP304 experience).
opportunities.next_action: Contact the CGIAR System Organization GCF focal point about re-accreditation plans and the internal pipeline; shortlist 1-2 countries with NDAs open to a CGIAR-led concept.

opportunities.title: Cambridge Africa Climate Collaborative Research Fund 2026/27 (Mastercard Foundation - University of Cambridge Climate Resilience and Sustainability Research Fund, round 3)
opportunities.funder: Mastercard Foundation (administered by University of Cambridge / Cambridge-Africa)
opportunities.program: Africa Climate Collaborative - Cambridge Africa Climate Collaborative Research Fund (formerly CReSus)
opportunities.deadline_text: The deadline for submission is 15th January 2027 and applications can be submitted at any time before this. Timeline: 15th October 2026 Applications open; 15th January 2027 Applications close; March 2027 Application outcomes confirmed.
opportunities.funding_text: Research Catalyst Grant for up to GBP 25,000, a Research Project Grant for up to GBP 80,000 or a Workshop Grant for up to GBP 50,000. We do not cover salaries of either investigator, institutional overheads, indirect costs or grant administration costs. Overall fund: GBP 7.7 million from the Mastercard Foundation, 2025-2030.
opportunities.duration: Approx. 12 months (Catalyst and Workshop grants) or up to 18 months (Research Project Grant); no-cost extensions up to 6 months considered
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Pairs of researchers (post-doctoral level or above; equivalent experience considered): one from the University of Cambridge (lead, administers the award) and one from a university or research institution of comparable standing on the African continent. Both must be employed at their institutions.
opportunities.eligible_countries: African partner: any country on the African continent; lead must be University of Cambridge
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Cannot lead (Cambridge applicant is always lead). The Alliance could be the Africa-based partner only via a researcher employed at an Alliance office in Africa (e.g., Nairobi) and only if accepted as a 'research institution of comparable standing to a university' - not stated explicitly; confirm with africaclimatecollaborative@cambridge-africa.cam.ac.uk. A Cali-based researcher cannot be the African applicant. Salaries and overheads not covered.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Cambridge-based applicant leads for administrative purposes, registers and invites the Africa-based applicant.
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: Research relevant to climate resilience and sustainability on the African continent; equipment must remain with the African institution.
opportunities.consortium_details: Mandatory Cambridge + African institution pair; true collaboration required. Research Project Grants require evidence of prior successful collaboration.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Seed/catalyst research, larger collaborative research projects, skills workshops in Africa; equipment for use in Africa.
opportunities.required_documents: Case for support; itemised budget; lay summary; letters of support from both departments/institutions; CVs; suggested referees.
opportunities.application_procedure: Online joint application form on the Cambridge-Africa website, started by the Cambridge applicant who invites the African applicant.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Climate resilience interpreted broadly; accommodates EO/AI crop monitoring, yield forecasting, climate-smart agriculture in Africa.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Builds a Cambridge partnership and Africa capacity; small amounts, no salary/overhead coverage.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Seed/workshop formats (e.g., GEE/EO training workshop) easily deliverable.
opportunities.recommendation: Pursue only if an Africa-based Alliance colleague and a Cambridge counterpart can be lined up before mid-December 2026; confirm Alliance eligibility as African institution first.
opportunities.potential_partners: University of Cambridge (Geography, Plant Sciences, Computer Science/AI for Environmental Risks), Alliance Africa hub (Nairobi), Makerere, University of Ghana, UCT
opportunities.next_action: Email africaclimatecollaborative@cambridge-africa.cam.ac.uk to confirm whether an Alliance Africa office qualifies; identify a Cambridge lead in November 2026.

opportunities.title: Horizon Europe Adaptation Mission: Researching and applying the potential of AI to foster climate resilience at regional and local levels (HORIZON-MISS-2027-01-CLIMA-02)
opportunities.program: Horizon Europe - EU Mission on Adaptation to Climate Change (Work Programme 2026-2027, call HORIZON-MISS-2027-01)
opportunities.deadline_text: Forthcoming; planned opening 9 Feb 2027; single-stage deadline 21 Sep 2027 (official portal topic data, status 'Forthcoming').
opportunities.funding_text: Indicative budget EUR 12,000,000 (2027); expected 4 grants; EU contribution EUR 3,000,000 per project. HORIZON-RIA, Lump Sum Grant.
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Standard Horizon Europe consortium rules (Annex B of General Annexes); no topic-specific restriction on participation.
opportunities.eligible_countries: EU Member States and Associated Countries; low/middle-income countries per Annex B; tools must be tested with European regional/local authorities.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: No topic-specific IO exception. Under Annex B, international organisations are funded only in specific cases; Bioversity International (HQ Rome, Italy) is the more plausible Alliance entity to participate; CIAT (Colombia) would at best be an associated partner. Topic targets European regions/local authorities (Objective 1: test with >=3; Objective 2: >=5 regional/local authorities, engaging private sector, e.g. smart agriculture), so the Alliance would be a technical partner (AI/EO for agricultural adaptation) rather than coordinator. Confirm Alliance legal status/PIC with grants office.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Standard HE RIA (min. 3 independent entities from 3 different MS/AC, at least one from a MS).
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: Use cases in European regions/local authorities.
opportunities.consortium_details: Consortium must engage regional/local authorities (>=3 for Obj. 1, >=5 for Obj. 2) and private-sector actors (Obj. 2); link with Mission Implementation Platform, UNDERPIN, CLIMAAX.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Objective 1 'AI for more accessible data' (deep learning to make climate data accessible for regional decision-making, possibly using Destination Earth); Objective 2 'AI for sectoral adaptation' (ML tools for resource management in sectors such as smart agriculture, water management); training and dissemination.
opportunities.required_documents: Standard HE application form (Part A/B) and detailed lump-sum budget table via the Funding & Tenders Portal.
opportunities.application_procedure: Submit via the EU Funding & Tenders Portal once open (planned 9 Feb 2027).
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: AI/ML for climate adaptation, climate data accessibility and smart agriculture directly matches RS/AI/climate-ag skills.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Europe-focused use cases; limited fit with Alliance LAC/Africa/Asia mission; partner role only.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Team has AI/EO and crop/climate modelling capability; needs a European consortium.
opportunities.recommendation: Consider only as a technical partner (via Bioversity International, Italy) in a European consortium targeting Objective 2 (smart agriculture); low priority otherwise.
opportunities.potential_partners: European universities/regional agencies in Italy/Spain; CMCC; Wageningen; regional authorities; agri-tech SMEs
opportunities.next_action: Check with Alliance grants office whether Bioversity International can be a funded beneficiary; scout European consortia before opening (Feb 2027).
